why_this_artifact_decides: DB9 failed because channel NAMES were right and the numbers were not. This artifact asks, for every mapped DOF, WHERE THE NUMBER PHYSICALLY COMES FROM

category.value: INSTRUMENTED GLOVE DIRECT or GLOVE + CALIBRATION TRANSFORM
category.source: handcorpus HUST page names a CyberGlove; no calibration procedure is obtainable

calibration_documented.note: the associated paper is RETRACTED and its methods cannot carry a calibration claim; no data was obtainable to measure the pipeline

dip_directly_measured_or_inferred.note: the page gives only a DOF count (16), not a channel list, so even whether DIP channels exist is unknown

HUST.verdict: ANGLE ORIGIN INDETERMINATE.  This is the DB9 situation with the additional defect that the associated publication was RETRACTED and the raw data cannot be obtained, so the indeterminacy cannot be reduced

category.source: Mendeley record: CyberGlove instrumented gloves, both hands, 18 DoF each, 'calibrated recordings'; the calibration pipeline is the BE-UJI code, which this audit downloaded and read

equipment.value: CyberGlove instrumented gloves, both hands, 18 DoF per hand

calibration_documented.value: YES - a full published protocol plus released code

per_subject_calibration.value: NO - gains are per GLOVE UNIT, applied across subjects.  The protocol is literally called 'across-subject calibration'

universal_coefficients.value: the released gains_identification.m hard-codes the UJI group's own glove gains, with per-model (CyberGlove 18 vs 22) and per-hand (R/L) sets, and states in a comment 'Gains values should be completed with own glove gains'

hand_size_dependence_discussed.value: YES, and unusually explicitly: the guide attributes a removed-outlier cluster to 'a poor fit of these gauges for a specific subject ... who had a small hand length'

cross_talk_discussed.value: YES - documented and MODELLED, not merely acknowledged: the protocol 'includes the determination of gains and also some corrections because of cross-coupling effects for specific anatomical angles', and the code implements explicit cross-coupling terms
cross_talk_discussed.source: MOVMUS guide section 2.1; obtain_angles_RL_abd_rel.m lines 120-121 (CMC1_F/CMC1_A 2x2 mix), 128-129 / 136-137 / 143-144 (MCP2_a / MCP4_a / MCP5_a quadratics in the neighbouring MCP flexion), 177-178 (wrist quadratic + cross term)

dip_directly_measured_or_inferred.value: INFERRED, and the group published a dedicated paper on the problem: for the 18-sensor glove the code computes DIP2..DIP5 from PIP2..PIP5 as a clipped affine map (0.87*PIP-25.27 and analogues, zero below a threshold).  A separate UJI dataset is titled 'Problems Using Data Gloves with Strain Gauges to Measure Distal Interphalangeal Joints' Kinematics'

calibration_quality_metrics.value: PARTIAL - the cited calibration paper provides them and the guide reports an outlier-removal procedure, but the per-recording residuals were not obtainable within the bounded-download rule

value.note: from the released KIN-MUS block, which shares the pipeline

KINE_ADL.verdict: PROVENANCE IS DOCUMENTED AND AUDITABLE, with two concrete limitations: (i) calibration is per GLOVE UNIT and applied across subjects, which the group itself links to a small-hand outlier cluster; (ii) DIP is a clipped affine function of PIP, so DIP carries no independent information

category.value: GLOVE + CALIBRATION TRANSFORM (identical pipeline to KINE_ADL)
category.source: Scientific Data 2019 abstract: 'Eighteen hand anatomical angles were obtained from the glove sensors by a validated calibration procedure'

equipment.value: CyberGlove instrumented glove + surface EMG; 18 angles; 7 forearm sEMG areas

shares_pipeline_with_KINE_ADL.value: YES - same research group (Biomechanics and Ergonomics, Universitat Jaume I), same glove family, same BE-UJI angle calculation code, same published calibration protocol

dip_directly_measured_or_inferred.value: INFERRED, and the KIN-MUS released angles do not include DIP at all

measured_channel_class_behaviour.value: as KINE_ADL - same code, same channel classes

KIN_MUS.verdict: PROVENANCE IS DOCUMENTED AND AUDITABLE.  Identical to KINE-ADL, which is exactly why the two are NOT independent sources of physical evidence

cross_dataset_origin_comparison.none_of_the_audited_candidates_uses_moti: all three audited candidates are strain-gauge glove datasets.  emg2pose, by contrast, is an inverse-kinematics fit of a generic hand model to motion capture.  THAT is the fundamental metrological difference this audit is measuring, and it is the same difference that broke DB9
what_makes_the_UJI_family_better_than_DB: the calibration protocol is published and the code is released, so the transform is auditable rather than proprietary
cross-coupling is explicitly modelled for named channels
the reference posture is documented with a figure
the sign criteria for every channel are published
the outlier-removal procedure and its counts are disclosed
a malfunctioning channel was detected and DISCLOSED
what_remains_weak_in_the_UJI_family: the gain transform is linear/quadratic in the raw gauge value and calibrated on ONE glove unit, not per subject
DIP is a clipped affine function of PIP and carries no independent information
the thumb IP channel reuses a PIP gain constant
a small-hand subject was identified as an outlier source, the same failure axis DB9 documented
whether the released KIN-MUS block is the right or the left hand is not labelled

db9_contrast.db9_outcome: DB9-DROP; 11 of 16 channels failed a DB9-only directional/repeatability screen
db9_contrast.relevance: DB9 is cited here ONLY as the reason the admission criteria and this artifact exist.  No DB9 measurement is used as evidence about the three candidates
